Synopsis:
Kevin Warsh's Fed faces a divided FOMC in a stagflationary environment: inflation remains well above the 2% target (PCE at 3.7% in June 2026), driven by war-related energy shocks, tariffs, and AI investment, while the labor market is softening. Recent cooler CPI and PPI prints have killed near-term rate hike bets for the Sep 15-16 meeting, but markets still price >90% probability of at least one hike by year-end. Three FOMC members dissented in favor of an immediate hike last meeting; hawks cite embedded inflation expectations risk. Doves argue shocks are transitory. The base case is an extended hold, with the Fed navigating between Trump's rate-cut pressure and internal hawks demanding action.
